description: ShellTask and ShellResult rules. Each case starts a shell with `args` and `kwargs`, then runs `steps` as Python. The steps see `sh` (the handle), `view`, and `door` (the call that started the shell) and put the result in `answer`. `expect` is the answer of `vis.shell` in the engine. The engine test `shell-handle-contract-test` runs each case in a real extension worker through `vis.shell` and `vis.tools.shell`. Both return an SDK Future. The SDK test `test_shell_contract.py` runs each case on the host outside Vis. Where one door answers differently, the case has a `tools` or `outside` object with a `reason` (a key of `exceptions`) and its own `expect`. The Python `runner` also accepts a sandbox ShellTask. A handle id in an answer shows as '<id>'.

exceptions.pipe: Outside Vis, a child process has pipes and no terminal. A line ends with one byte, typed text has no echo, `type` needs a command that started with `stdin: tty`, and Ctrl-D does not end the input.
exceptions.sh: Outside Vis, the command runs with `/bin/sh -c`. The engine runs it with `bash -lc`.
exceptions.raw-op: `vis.tools.shell` starts a command or attaches to a running alias. It does not take the raw logs or send operations.
exceptions.op-key: The answer of the `shell` tool has the `op` key. The SDK handle does not have it.
exceptions.local: Outside Vis, no session holds the shell. `attach` is empty, `note` says that the command is a local process, and `keys` is empty after `type`.
exceptions.roots: `vis.tools.shell` is the `shell` tool of the model. It keeps the working directory in the filesystem roots of the session, and it checks that first.
exceptions.guest-wait: The guest Task has wait(seconds). The SDK Future has result(timeout), which raises TimeoutError if the command is still running.
exceptions.other-origin: Outside Vis, there is no second active session tool with a separate trust origin.
